text: Managed Instance needs everything Azure SQL Database needs, plus one hard requirement: a dedicated subnet inside a Virtual Network, delegated specifically to it. That network isolation is what makes near-full SQL Server surface possible on a PaaS product.

This is the real Portal screen for configuring a new Managed Instance's compute and storage — the same vCore choices from Lesson 9, scoped to an instance, plus the VNet and subnet selection required before you can even reach it.

Provisioning a new Managed Instance commonly takes four to six hours, sometimes longer — not the minute or two Azure SQL Database needed. That's the real provisioning time behind its near-full SQL Server surface with PaaS patching.
This is exactly what you should expect to see for hours after clicking create — a deployment-in-progress status, not an error. Never assume a deployment still running after twenty minutes has failed.
There's nothing to click or fix while it runs. Confirm the subnet has no conflicts, prepare firewall and NSG rules ahead of time, and draft the migration plan you'll execute once it's up.
Next up: SQL Server on Azure VMs and hybrid SQL — the full-IaaS option, and Azure Hybrid Benefit applied to licensing directly.
